text: Four and a half thousand years ago, while Egypt built its pyramids,
a city on the Indus had drains under every street.
With Harappa, it was the heart of the Indus Valley Civilisation.
Bricks were baked to the same proportions.
Most homes had their own bathroom.
Merchants stamped their goods with seals,
in a script no one can read, to this day.
the monsoon weakened, and the cities emptied.
Four thousand years later, archaeologists dug into a mound called Mohenjo-daro.
